title: Memory reservation profiles for KV streaming and activation spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Deliver a set of configurable memory reservation profiles that balance weights, KV cache, and activations for streaming inference workloads using continuous batching. The goal is to provide per-tenant "profiles" (conservative / balanced / aggressive) that the admission controller and headroom planner can use to decide admission, prefetch, and eviction priorities. This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation of reservation enforcement, and observability:
- Define reservation model: fixed weight reservation, soft KV reservation, activation working set margin, and emergency spillover thresholds.
- Admission control integration: use profile to compute an admission budget per request and signal backpressure or preferred model variant (smaller context/quantized).
- Continuous batching interaction: adjust reservation dynamically based on live batch composition and latency SLOs.
- Eviction & prefetch policy: define priority order and decay rules for tenant-scoped KV entries.
- Telemetry & alerts: per-profile dashboards, p99/p50 token latencies, eviction rates, spill events, and headroom trend charts.
- Compatibility: support pinned weights, multi-model pools, and fallback to quantized variants if headroom cannot be satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation profiles documented in Confluence with precise formulas and config knobs
Admission controller consults profile and rejects/defers requests when budget exceeded (configurable thresholds)
Simulation harness demonstrates >=30% reduction in KV eviction spikes for balanced profile vs current baseline on mixed workloads
Dashboard shows per-profile headroom utilization, eviction rates, and correlates with latency SLO violations
Implementation includes a safety override to fall back to quantized smaller model when spill risk >80%
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike showed frequent KV churn on interleaved short/long requests. Initial offline profiling attached to Confluence page.

2025-02-12 - Ethan Brooks: Ran batch simulator for mixed chat+completion workload. Observed eviction cascades when long-chat tokens intermixed with high-concurrency short requests. Baseline eviction rate 18% (per-window).

2025-02-13 - Design review (Marina Gomez): Recommend soft reservation for KV with decay-based replenishment to avoid starvation; prefer per-tenant windows rather than global quotas to improve fairness.

2025-02-15 - Spike result: conservative profile (weight: 95%, kv_soft: 2.5GB, activation_margin: 10%) reduced spill events but increased tail latency for very large requests. Balanced profile reduces eviction spikes without noticeable p99 increase.

2025-02-17 - Engineering decision: implement three profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with tunable knobs. Integrate a headroom predictor that uses exponential smoothing over recent batch compositions.

2025-02-18 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234. Implements reservation enforcement and exposes metrics (headroom_util, kv_evictions, spill_count) via runtime telemetry.

2025-02-19 - QA notes (Liam O'Connor): Found race when evicting tenant KV entries during near-simultaneous admission rejections. Added mitigation: serialized eviction window + fast-path check. Added unit tests.
2025-02-20 - Product feedback (Sofia Chen): Add a migration guide for existing Dedicated customers; default to 'balanced' profile and expose opt-in for 'aggressive' on dedicated pools only.
